items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Piano. I'll tell you about him. James Hemingway.

ctx.x: Piano. I'll tell you about him. James Hemingway. James Hemingway. And bass and all that. I really hadn't forgotten now, he was changing up so much. But I know they had a little fellow down on the drum named Buck. He was here a long time, stayed in New Orleans a good while. Bucket they called him. And Popeye on Alto. I can't call them guys names now that I wanted. But the guys was with him.
Did you ever hear Eva and Thomas and Bunk play together?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Yeah, James Hemingway. That was his name, James Hemingway. And he made the record, huh? Yeah, he made the record.

ctx.x: Who was the piano player with Mac and Mac? You remember that record you made with Mac and Mac?
Yeah, James Hemingway. That was his name, James Hemingway. And he made the record, huh? Yeah, he made the record.
What trumpet players had the best syncopation and rhythm and all that in those times?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Hemingway, James Hemingway. Hemingway. Yeah, James Hemingway. Now he was a good piano player.

ctx.x: Did Morris Rouse ever work with him? Who? Morris Rouse, Rouse, what can I pronounce it, Rouse or Rouse? Never knew him, huh?
Hemingway, James Hemingway. Hemingway. Yeah, James Hemingway. Now he was a good piano player.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: He played with us a couple of years, but he didn't live alone.

ctx.x: There's a Henry Brown that plays blues living in St. Louis now. Can you see him? I don't know. I don't know. I'll tell you how I find out about it. Roosevelt Sykes told me about it, you know. Might be him.
I don't know. Never got to know his father from Atlanta. Well, he died pretty soon. His name was Hemingway, James Hemingway. He played with us a couple of years, but he didn't live alone. He died.
Was he a trumpet player? No, piano. Piano player.
